title: Camouflage screenshot scenarios
description: One list of scenarios drives the screenshot suites of Kotlin (Roborazzi), Dart (Alchemist) and web (Playwright over Storybook), so the three can be compared name by name. A scenario is a component in one configuration; it expands over skins, modes, text scales and directions.

defaults.description: The axes a scenario takes when it does not narrow them.

name.description: Unique, lowercase, dash-separated: the first part of every file name (`button-solid-error`).

component.description: The component's name without prefix (`button`); on the web the element is `camo-<component>`.

props.description: The component's parameters by their contract names (camelCase in Kotlin and Dart, kebab-case attributes on the web). A string or number is a value, `true` is a present boolean, `false` is absent.

content.description: What goes in the slots: the key is the slot name (`""` for the default slot), the value a plain string for text or HTML for the web; Kotlin and Dart map the same keys to their slot parameters.

frame.description: `element` captures the component's own box; `page` captures a fixed viewport, for overlays that leave the flow.
